title: Common Risk Factors in Decentralized AI Subnets

extraction.methodology_summary: Daily subnet data from the Taostats API is used to construct lagged characteristics including market capitalization, momentum, emission yield, and liquidity for decentralized AI subnet tokens priced via constant-product AMMs. Portfolios are formed daily using tercile sorts on these lagged characteristics, and long-short factor returns are calculated as the difference between extreme terciles. Fama-MacBeth cross-sectional regressions, GRS tests, and spanning tests are conducted to evaluate the factor structure.
extraction.universe: 128 decentralized AI subnet tokens on the Bittensor network, excluding subnet 0 and subnets in startup mode

performance_metrics.evidence_quote: The size factor (SMB) is the strongest: small subnets outperform large subnets by 1.01% per day, with a Newey-West t-statistic of 3.28 (OLS t = 4.04) and an annualized Sharpe ratio of 3.84.
The 30-day momentum factor earns 0.68% per day (NW t = 3.69, Sharpe 4.32)
and the 7-day variant earns 0.75% (NW t = 3.05, Sharpe 3.65).
The market factor earns 0.29% per day in TAO terms, reflecting the general appreciation of subnet tokens over the sample period. The annualized Sharpe ratio is 1.35.

key_findings: A size effect (small-minus-big, SMB) dominates the cross-section, earning 1.01% per day with a Newey-West t-statistic of 3.28.
Momentum is pervasive, with 30-day and 7-day winning-minus-losing portfolios earning 0.68% and 0.75% daily, respectively.
The December 2025 halving of token emissions reduced the size premium from 1.17% to 0.51% daily, consistent with a structural constant-product AMM pricing mechanism.
Constant-product AMM slippage causes the size premium to be implementable only for portfolio AUM below $10K, as transaction costs exceed gross returns at $100K and above.
limitations: The sample period is short (13 months).
Transaction costs in thin AMM pools severely erode paper returns at higher AUM levels.
